nodes.title: Product runtime turn-taking, held-out TEST split, before the fix: she cut in during a caller's mid-thought pause on 32.7% of turns (18/55, 95% CI 0.22-0.46) and talked over the caller on 25.5% (14/55, 0.16-0.38). End of turn to her first audio: median 1000 ms, including 450 ms of fixed fake provider time. Barge-in: 2/55 missed, she yields in a median 725 ms. Backchannel and noise false barge-ins: 0/55 each
nodes.method:
product/voice/bench/turn_bench.py --split test --set STATEMENT_HOLD_MS=0, 2026-10-23, Python 3.13, Silero VAD, in real time.
- Clips: 102 synthetic Hinglish caller clips (research/2026-10-17/lanes/l8-azure-bench/stimuli, phone band, with their text), split DEV/TEST by a hash of the clip id (47 DEV / 55 TEST).
- Labels: speech regions from each clip's energy envelope (-38 dBFS, gaps under 150 ms bridged); internal pauses of 250 ms or more count as mid-thought pauses.
- Runtime: the real cascade turn logic (VAD, held and withdrawn replies, barge-in).
- Fakes, fixed timing: the final arrives 250 ms after the VAD's end of speech, with words snapped to punctuation at pauses; brain 300 ms; voice 150 ms to first audio; no echo.
- Scenarios: turn (a whole clip, which always ends in a question); statement (the clip cut after its last full stop, 50 turns); barge (the caller starts 2 s into her long opening); backchannel (a 300 ms vocal burst, and separately a 300 ms burst of noise at -30 dBFS).
- CIs: Wilson for proportions, bootstrap for medians.
- Not measured: real ASR finals, real providers, echo, real callers, telephone jitter.
nodes.value: premature cut-in 32.7% of turns, talk-over 25.5% (TEST, n=55)

nodes.title: A 1200 ms hold after a caller's statement (chosen on DEV) cuts premature cut-ins on held-out TEST from 32.7% to 3.6% of turns (2/55, 95% CI 0.01-0.12) and talk-over from 25.5% to 3.6%. The cost: turns that end in a statement get her first audio at a median 1314 ms instead of 986 ms (+328 ms, n=49/41). Question-ended turns are unchanged (998 ms). Barge-in, backchannel and noise handling are unchanged
nodes.method:
Same bench, --split test, defaults after the change (STATEMENT_HOLD_MS=1200), 2026-10-23.
- DEV sweep over 0/600/1000/1200/1400 (bench/results/turn-2026-10-23-dev-sweep.md): premature cut-ins 40% / 38% / 19% / 2% / 2%; statement latency 977 / 979 / 1116 / 1308 / 1493 ms. 1200 was chosen on DEV and is reported on TEST only.
- Cause, traced on a DEV clip: the hold is counted from the end of the caller's speech, but the transcript lands about 410 ms later, so a 0 ms hold after a sentence that reads complete releases her reply inside 0.3-1.4 s mid-thought pauses.
- The speculative reply is generated while she waits, so with real providers (slower than the fakes) more of the hold hides behind generation. Not measured.
- Caveat: the stimuli end every whole turn in a question, so the question fast path (HOLD_MS=0) is favoured by this set; the statement scenario exists to show the cost.
nodes.value: premature cut-in 3.6%, talk-over 3.6% (TEST, n=55); +328 ms after statements

nodes.title: The cascade's held reply waits by how the caller's words end: no hold after a question (it hands her the turn); 1200 ms of silence after a statement; 1400 ms after an unfinished turn (a trailing comma or connective)
nodes.rationale: measure.2026-10-23.turn-taking-statement-hold: cut-ins and talk-over fall from about 1 in 3 turns to about 1 in 28 on held-out clips, at +328 ms only after statements.
nodes.reverse_if: on real calls (the India VM bench with real ASR, or live test calls) the statement wait is felt as slow, or cut-ins stay low with a shorter hold because real ASR finals arrive at a different time; or a semantic end-of-turn model beats punctuation

nodes.title: She yields to a caller who talks over her in a median 725 ms (TEST, n=55, 95% CI 708-739), and missed 2/55 barge-ins within 1.5 s. People yield in about 200-400 ms. Lowering BARGE_MS / BARGE_LONG_MS speeds this up but risks false barge-ins on backchannels and noise (0/55 each today). Next lever to bench on DEV
nodes.closes_when: a DEV-tuned barge-in rule lowers the yield time on TEST without raising false barge-ins, or the real-provider bench shows 725 ms is not felt
